c.tagline: Belle Époque grandeur meets gritty, garden-filled energy.

taxi.fareNote: Only use taxis with a company logo, meter, and posted per-km rate on the door (avoid unmarked cabs, especially at the airport); Uber and Bolt are typically cheaper and more reliable

emergency.note: 112 covers police, fire, and ambulance nationwide; English-speaking operators are usually available

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing on transit and around Gara de Nord; taxi overcharging — use apps

hood_desc: Cobblestoned historic core packed with bars, clubs, cafes and restored 19th-century facades; best for first-timers and nightlife-seekers who want to walk everywhere.
Grand central boulevard lined with museums, government buildings and shopping; suits business travelers and culture-focused visitors who want a central, well-connected base.

Leafy district around Bucharest's largest park and lake, with joggers, cafes and a family-friendly feel; suits travelers wanting quiet greenery and easy access to the northern airport road, a bit removed from nightlife.
Upscale residential enclave with embassies, boutiques and trendy restaurants; suits travelers seeking a chic, quieter base with excellent dining nearby.
Central area anchored by Unirii Square and the massive Palace of Parliament, well served by metro; suits budget travelers and those wanting proximity to major sights and transit hubs.

water.note: Meets EU standards and is safe to drink, though a chlorine smell leads many to prefer bottled water.

transit.pay: Contactless bank cards can be tapped directly on metro gates and STB surface vehicles. Single tickets, day passes and the rechargeable Activ/Bucharest City Card are also sold at station kiosks and vending machines. Keep a validated ticket or tapped card for random inspections on trams and buses.
transit.hours: Metro runs roughly 05:00-23:00; trams, buses and trolleybuses operate similar daytime hours with a limited network of night buses covering major routes after midnight
transit.note: Metro line M1 forms an inner ring, M2 runs north-south through the center, and newer lines M4/M5 extend service; surface trams and buses fill gaps well

train: CFR Călători national and international trains from Gara de Nord
bus: FlixBus and other international coaches serving Autogara Militari and Autogara Berceni

transit.m: Bus 780 express to Piața Unirii (~45 min)
Henri Coandă Express train to Gara de Nord (~25 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving 10% at restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory; not customary for taxis

food.name: Mici (mititei)
food.desc: Skinless grilled sausages of beef, lamb and pork with garlic, pepper and a fizz of soda water; eaten with mustard, bread and cold beer.

places.name: Terasa Obor
places.note: No-frills terrace at Obor market grilling mici all day; the city's benchmark.

places.name: Caru' cu Bere
places.note: Neo-gothic beer hall from 1879; touristy but the mici and atmosphere deliver.

places.name: Hanu' lui Manuc
places.note: Early 19th-century inn courtyard, good for a grill platter and live music.

food.name: Sarmale
food.desc: Cabbage or vine leaves rolled around minced pork and rice, slow-cooked with smoked meat and served with mamaliga, sour cream and hot pepper.

places.name: Caru' cu Bere
places.note: Classic sarmale with polenta in a landmark dining room; book at peak times.

places.name: Vatra
places.note: Warm folk-styled restaurant focused on well-seasoned home-style Romanian cooking.

places.name: La Mama
places.note: Reliable local chain doing the 'like at mum's' version at fair prices.

food.name: Ciorba de burta
food.desc: Creamy sour tripe soup finished with garlic, egg yolk and sour cream, sharpened at the table with vinegar and hot peppers. A legendary hangover cure.

places.name: Lacrimi si Sfinti
places.note: Modern Romanian kitchen using heritage produce; repeatedly praised for its ciorba.

places.name: Locanta Jaristea
places.note: Belle-epoque dining room with traditional soups and live period music.

places.name: Caru' cu Bere
places.note: Serves the full ciorba range including burta and perisoare all day.

food.name: Papanasi
food.desc: Fried doughnut of sweet cow's cheese topped with a doughnut hole, sour cream and sour-cherry jam. Order one for two people.

places.name: Caru' cu Bere
places.note: Its papanasi is the most photographed dessert in Bucharest, and still good.

places.name: Hanu' lui Manuc
places.note: Generous courtyard version with plenty of visinata cherry jam.

places.name: Vatra
places.note: Home-style papanasi in a quieter room than the Old Town landmarks.

food.name: Tochitura with mamaliga
food.desc: Pork and sausage stewed in wine and garlic, served over polenta with a fried egg and grated telemea sheep cheese on top.

places.name: Zexe Zahana
places.note: Restaurant reviving pre-war Bucharest recipes and its own charcuterie.

places.name: Hanu' lui Manuc
places.note: Hearty inn cooking; the tochitura arrives in a clay pot with mamaliga.

places.name: Caru' cu Bere
places.note: Menu staple alongside the grill; large portions, brisk service.

food.name: Covrigi
food.desc: Hot Bucharest pretzel rings, plain or crusted with salt, poppy or sesame, sold from corner windows and eaten walking down the street.

places.name: Luca
places.note: Popular covrigarie chain baking continuously; join the queue for the hot batch.

places.name: Obor Market stalls
places.note: Market bakers sell covrigi and placinta alongside the mici terraces.

places.name: Gara de Nord kiosks
places.note: Station-area windows are the classic cheap covrigi stop at any hour.

food.name: Tuica and palinca
food.desc: Home-distilled plum brandy: tuica is softer, palinca is double-distilled and fierce. Served chilled or warmed as a pre-meal shot.

places.name: Caru' cu Bere
places.note: House tuica served in small carafes, the traditional way to open a meal.

places.name: Zexe Zahana
places.note: Selection of regional tuica and palinca matched to the charcuterie.

places.name: Hanu' lui Manuc
places.note: Courtyard inn pouring plum brandy alongside the grill menu.

food.name: Romanian wine
food.desc: Native grapes worth seeking out: red Feteasca Neagra, aromatic white Feteasca Regala and Tamaioasa Romaneasca from Dealu Mare and Recas.

places.name: Abel's Wine Bar
places.note: Bucharest wine bar with a deep Romanian list and knowledgeable pours by the glass.

places.name: Locanta Jaristea
places.note: Old-school cellar list heavy on Romanian estates, matched to traditional food.

places.name: Caru' cu Bere
places.note: Easy place to sample house Romanian wine by the carafe with a meal.

landmarks: Palace of the Parliament
The second-largest administrative building in the world, this colossal Communist-era palace is Bucharest's most jaw-dropping architectural spectacle.
Romanian Athenaeum
An exquisite neoclassical concert hall with a domed facade that has become the definitive symbol of Bucharest's cultural elegance.
Arcul de Triumf (Arch of Triumph)
Modeled after the Parisian original, this triumphal arch commemorates Romania's WWI reunification and anchors a grand boulevard.
CEC Palace
An ornate Beaux-Arts landmark with a glass-and-steel dome, long considered one of the most beautiful buildings on Bucharest's historic Calea Victoriei.
Stavropoleos Monastery
A tiny, exquisitely detailed 18th-century Orthodox church tucked into the Old Town, prized for its ornate Brâncovenesc-style carvings.
Curtea Veche (Old Princely Court)
The ruined medieval court of Vlad the Impaler, complete with his statue, forming the historic heart of Bucharest's Old Town.
Village Museum (Muzeul Satului)
An open-air museum of authentic wooden farmhouses and churches relocated from across Romania, set on the shore of Herăstrău Lake.
Herăstrău Park (King Michael I Park)
Bucharest's largest and most scenic park, wrapped around a picturesque lake and a favorite spot for lakeside photos.
Revolution Square
The historic square where the 1989 revolution against Ceaușescu unfolded, marked by the striking Memorial of Rebirth.
Cișmigiu Gardens
Bucharest's oldest and most romantic public park, with a picturesque lake, willow-lined paths, and classic 19th-century landscaping.

train.note: All international trains leave from Gara de Nord (Bucharest North). The Dacia, Ister and Prietenia sleepers run year-round, but the Istanbul overnight couchette car and the Sofia/Varna day trains are summer-only (in 2026: 12 June to 12 October). Bring your passport - border checks happen on board or at the frontier.

bus.note: Bucharest has no single central coach terminal - international buses leave from several different terminals and stops around the city (some also call at Otopeni airport), so check the exact departure point on your ticket.

ferry.note: Bucharest is an inland city with no passenger ferry services. The nearby Danube crossing to Bulgaria at Giurgiu-Ruse is a road and rail bridge, and even Constanța on the Black Sea coast has no regular international passenger ferries.

half.name: Sinaia (Peleș Castle)
half.blurb: A fairytale royal palace set among forested peaks in an alpine resort town.

half.name: Râșnov
half.blurb: A hilltop peasant citadel offering sweeping views over the Carpathian countryside.

half.name: Bușteni
half.blurb: A mountain village with cable cars climbing to the dramatic Bucegi plateau.

full.name: Brașov
full.blurb: A medieval Saxon city with a gothic church and colorful old-town square.

full.name: Bran Castle
full.blurb: The dramatic clifftop fortress popularly linked to the legend of Dracula.

full.name: Constanța
full.blurb: An ancient port city blending Roman ruins with breezy Black Sea beaches.
